verdict: Caution: lend selectively in Bhiwadi engineering & capital goods — favour component/machining SMEs with diversified, non-Rajasthan order books and tight monthly discipline; avoid single-shift gas-dependent units and pure local-order fabricators.
title: Bhiwadi Engineering & Capital Goods: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**Bhiwadi's engineering units convert steel, copper and bought-out castings into components, structures and machined parts, and cash comes back only after the buyer accepts and pays.** Value sits in the order book and the buyer relationship, not the machine; capex is moderate but lumpy, and the working-capital cycle is the real risk because EPC-linked buyers pay slowly [9][11]. **So when a proposal lands, check the order book's customer mix and payment terms before you look at the P&L.**

## What has changed now
**The national demand signal is strong but the local one is not.** India-wide NIC 28 output is +10.3% YoY and +10.4% Apr-to-date [D], yet Rajasthan GST collections are -4.7% Apr-to-date against India +6.1%, and state electricity demand is +4.0% against India +9.5% [D]. **Local reporting says 400 factories in the Bhiwadi belt are near closure with production halved and 25,000 jobs at risk, driven by a gas/energy crisis and single-shift running [3] — that is a local news report from April 2026, so treat it as dated but directionally serious.** Separately, RPCB has no lab in Bhiwadi to test iron and copper particulate pollution [2], which tells you compliance scrutiny on foundry-type units is likely to rise. **If a unit runs one shift on gas, ask for its gas contract and last six months' power and fuel cost per tonne before anything else.**

## Where the growth is
**Peer results show where demand actually is: data centres, mining, off-highway, railways and power T&D.** Pitti is commissioning a Hyderabad casting and machining facility through FY2030 on data-centre, mining, off-highway and railway order visibility [4]; Skipper posted its highest-ever Q2 revenue with PAT up 56% on T&D structures and exports [6]; DEE's order book crossed Rs 1,300 crore with Q3 revenue up 77% to Rs 286.7 crore [5]. **Pursue Bhiwadi component and machining SMEs that supply these chains — transmission structures, castings, machined parts — with at least part of the order book outside Rajasthan.** Avoid pure local-order fabricators and units whose entire output feeds one Rajasthan buyer.

## How to grow safely
**Structure for the working-capital cycle, not the balance sheet.** Take monthly stock and receivable statements, sanction working capital against a drawing power you recompute each month, and keep term loans short and matched to a named machine. **Take every month: GST returns, e-way bills, top-five buyer ledger, power and fuel bills, and a stock-and-receivable statement; if receivables days stretch beyond the sanctioned cycle, cut drawing power immediately.** Where bank guarantees are needed for bidding, size the non-fund limit to the bid pipeline and take the counter-guarantee properly [9]. **If the proposal is a greenfield expansion, ask for phase-wise commissioning and customer confirmation, as Pitti's phased Hyderabad plan shows [4].**

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the local, not the national, numbers.** A second consecutive month of falling GST in the unit's own filings, a shift from two shifts to one, or a buyer delaying beyond terms are the triggers. **Suzlon's Q2 FY27 shows volume growth with EBITDA margin down to 14.8% from 18.6% [7] — so if a borrower's revenue grows while margin falls, ask for the price-escalation clause in its contracts.** Any pollution notice or RPCB inspection letter on a foundry unit means stop and reassess [2]. **If the unit cannot show a gas or power contract beyond six months, decline.**
watch: GST turnover falls below e-way bill value for two months -> freeze drawing power and call for buyer confirmations
Power and fuel cost per tonne (monthly)
Cost rises while realisations flat -> ask for price-escalation clause; if none, reduce limit
Order book by customer and state (quarterly)
Rajasthan share rises above half the book -> reprice or decline fresh limits
Any inspection or notice on the unit -> stop disbursement and reassess [2]
